note: Frame-header parsing consumes attacker-controlled bytes from the input stream into the bitreader.
The UTF-8 continuation-byte check is wrong: it accepts bytes with bit 6 set, so malformed multi-byte sequences can be treated as valid and advance parsing state incorrectly.
On malformed UTF-8, the decoder rewinds using the last byte seen, preserving the misparsed header state for subsequent sync/search logic.

The decoder computes CRC over the over-extended raw_header buffer after the malformed UTF-8 path has appended extra bytes, which is the target invalid read path in the vulnerable frame-header handling.
